sentence: Under the terms of theActs of Union, the Kingdoms of England and Scotland merged to form theKingdom of Great Britain, with asingle parliamentand government based inWestminster.
Thesecret societyknown as theOrder of Illuminatiwas founded byAdam WeishauptandAdolph Freiherr KniggeinIngolstadt,Bavaria, Germany.
The originalChicago Board of Trade Buildingopened for business.
Adust explosionat a coal mine nearScofield, Utah, U.S.,killedat least 200 miners.
Sicilian separatistSalvatore Giulianoand his gangfired into a crowdofMay Daymarchers nearPiana degli Albanesi,Sicily, killing 11 and wounding 33.
InMajor League Baseball,Rickey Hendersonbroke the record forstolen baseson the same night thatNolan Ryanbroke his own record forno-hitters.
The evacuation of nearly 88,000 people began whena wildfireswept throughFort McMurray, Alberta, Canada, and burned for another 14 months, becoming the costliest disaster in Canadian history.
New York City'sEmpire State Building(pictured), at the time thetallest building in the world, opened.
Argentine presidentJuan PerónexpelledMontonerosfrom a demonstration in thePlaza de Mayoin Buenos Aires, forcing the group to become a clandestine organization.
Aroyal chartergranted theHudson's Bay Companya monopoly in thefur tradeinRupert's Land(present-day Canada).
TheChaiténvolcano in Chile began to erupt for the first time since around 1640.
TheConservative Party of Canadawon enough seats inthe federal electionto establish their firstmajority government.
TheTreaty of Wuchalewas signed, endingthe Italo-Ethiopian War, but differences in translation later led toanother war.
TheTreaty of Loudunwas signed, ending a war that originally began as a power struggle for the French throne.
TheGreat Sejmof thePolish–Lithuanian Commonwealthratifiedthe first codified national constitution in Europe.
A long-running feud between two towns inWisconsincame to a head when aschoonercrashed into a bridge; they later merged to form the city ofMilwaukee.
A group of Americanmercenariesled byWilliam Walkerset sail from San Francisco toconquer Nicaragua.
The oldestRoyal Air Forcestation in continuous operation,RAF Northolt, opened as home toNo. 4Reserve Aeroplane Squadron.
Under the BritishGovernment of Ireland Act,Ireland was partitionedinto two self-governing territories,NorthernandSouthern Ireland.
A newConstitution of Japanwent into effect, providing for aparliamentarysystem of government, guaranteeing certainfundamental rights, and relegating theJapanese monarchyto a purely ceremonial role.
TheOff-BroadwayshowThe Fantastickspremiered, eventually becoming the world's longest-running musical, with 17,162 performances across 42 years.
Police inBirmingham, Alabama,used high-pressure water hoses and dogsagainstcivil-rights protesters, bringing scrutiny onracial segregation in the southern United States.
TheKargil Warinitiates when Indian forces detected the infiltration of Pakistani forces in Indian-administeredKargil, a city inJammu and Kashmir.
Three-year-old British girlMadeleine McCann disappearedfrom a holiday apartment inPraia da Luz, Portugal; she has never been found.
United Kingdom general electionis saved forMay 4, the date of Margaret Thatcher officially becoming Prime Minister
TheBenty Grange helmet, a boar-crestedAnglo-Saxonhelmet with parallels to those mentioned in the contemporary epic poemBeowulf, was discovered inDerbyshire, England.
ADoppler on Wheelsteam measured the fastest winds recorded on Earth, at 143.6 m/s (321 mph; 517 km/h), ina tornadonearBridge Creek, Oklahoma.
TheBoydell Shakespeare Gallery, part of a cultural project initiated by engraverJohn Boydell, opened in London.
During alabor rallyin Chicago,a bomb explosion and gunfireled to the deaths of eight police officers and four members of the public.
TheParliament of Maltamoved from theGrandmaster's Palaceto the purpose-builtParliament House(pictured).
An all-female Japanese team reached the summit ofManasluin theHimalayas, becoming the first women to climb apeak higher than 8,000 metres (26,247 ft) above sea level.
stamp commemorating the Battle of the Wilderness
Led by Italian generalGiuseppe Garibaldi, the volunteerExpedition of the Thousandset sail fromGenoaon a campaign to conquer theKingdom of the Two Sicilies, a crucial event of theunification of Italy.
TheNetherlands Carillonwas inaugurated inArlington, Virginia, on the 15th anniversary ofDutch Liberation Day.
Aftera 66-day hunger strike, Irish republicanBobby Sandsdied of starvation inHM Prison Maze.
TheTwenty-seventh Amendment to the United States Constitutionwas ratified, 202 years after it was first proposed.
American teenagerMichael P. Faywascaned in Singaporefor theft and vandalism, a punishment that the United States deemed to be excessive for a teenager committing a non-violent crime.
Philippine broadcast networkABS-CBNwasforced to go off-airby theNational Telecommunications CommissionafterCongressfailed to renew its franchise granted in 1995.
The BritishSpecial Air Servicerecaptured theIranian embassy in Londonfollowinga six-day siegeafterIranian Arab separatistshad seized it.
English poetChristopher Smartwas admitted toSt Luke's Hospital for Lunaticsin London, beginninghis six-year confinementtomental asylums.
Irish civil servantsThomas Henry BurkeandLord Frederick Cavendishwere stabbed to deathby members of the radicalIrish National InvinciblesinPhoenix Park, Dublin.
U.S. presidentChester A. Arthursigned theChinese Exclusion Actinto law(cartoon pictured), implementing a ban onChinese immigration to the United Statesthat remained for 61 years.
The German airshipHindenburgcaught fire andwas destroyedduring an attempt to dock atLakehurst Naval Air StationinNew Jersey, killing 36 people.
American entertainerBob Hopeperformed his first show with theUnited Service Organizations, beginning a 50-year involvement with them.
AtOxford'sIffley Road Track, English runnerRoger Bannisterbecame the first person to run themile in under four minutes.
BritishbarristerMark Saunderswas shot dead by policeafter a five-hour siege at his home inChelsea, London.
Exacerbated byhigh-frequency tradersusing strategies that have since been banned, major U.S.stock indicesdropped nearly 9 percent and quickly rebounded.
Construction began on theGrand Palace(pictured)in Bangkok, the official residence of theking of Thailand.
Thefinal episodeof the television sitcomFriendswas aired.
Amanda Berry escaped from theCleveland, Ohio, home of her captor,Ariel Castro, having been held there with two other women for ten years.
lithograph of theCity of Adelaide
The 13th-century castle ofTre Kronorin Stockholm burned down; plans forthe current royal palacewere presented within the year.
A convoy of circus wagons carrying lions, horses, ponies and an ass lost control and overturned into some shop fronts inDungannon, Northern Ireland.
Police inNapier, New Zealand, begana 40-hour siegeof the home of a formerNew Zealand Armymember who had shot at officers during the routine execution of asearch warrant.
A draft sequence of theNeanderthalgenome was published, demonstrating thattoday's humans have Neanderthal ancestors.
Employees atFleischer Studiosin New York Citywent on strikein the animation industry's first major labor strike.
Lithuania signed theKlaipėda Convention, making theKlaipėda Region(taken fromEast Prussia) into an autonomous region under Lithuanian rule.

A parade inSétif,French Algeria, celebrating theend of WorldWar IIin Europebecame a riot and was followed byreprisals, carried out by colonial authorities over the following weeks, that killed thousands.
TheTollund Man(pictured), a naturally mummified corpse, was discovered in a peat bog nearSilkeborg, Denmark.
Construction workersattackedstudents and otherswho were protesting the Vietnam Warin New York City.
A BritishSpecial Air ServiceunitambushedaProvisional Irish Republican Army(IRA) unit inLoughgall, Northern Ireland, killing eight IRA members and one civilian.
A trainderailed and caught firenearVersailles, France, killing at least 52 people.
French aviatorsCharles NungesserandFrançois Coliaboard thebiplaneL'Oiseau Blanctook off from Paris, attempting to make the first non-stop flight to New York, only to disappear before arrival.
InHuế,South Vietnam, soldiersopened fireinto a crowd ofBuddhistsprotesting against a government ban on the flying of theBuddhist flagonPhật Đản, killing nine and sparking theBuddhist crisis.
Four members ofBlack SeptemberhijackedSabena Flight 571to demand the release of 315 Palestinians convicted on terrorism charges.
The U.S.Food and Drug Administrationannounced that it would approve the use ofSearle'sEnovid, the firstcombined oral contraceptive pill.
In a speech to U.S. broadcasters,FCCchairmanNewton Minowdescribed commercial television programming as "a vast wasteland".
About 200 students atBucks County Community Collegehelda protestafter the college canceled a planned speech by gay rights activistDick Leitsch.
ProminentIranian JewHabib Elghanianwas executed after having been convicted by arevolutionary tribunalof various charges, triggering a mass exodus of Jews from Iran.
An undergroundmethaneexplosion occurred at theWestray MineinPlymouth, Nova Scotia, killing all 26 Canadian coal miners who were working at the time.
The pilots of aSukhoi Superjet, ignoring alerts from theterrain warning system,crashed the aircraftintoMount Salakin Indonesia, resulting in the deaths of all 45 people on board.
The Hotel Polen inAmsterdamwasdestroyed by fire(pictured), leaving 33 people dead.
Part of theSunshine Skyway Bridgein Florida collapsed after a pier was struck byMVSummit Venture, killing 35 people.
Police at theOhene Djan Stadiumin Accra, Ghana, firedtear gasto quell unrest at a football match, leading toa stampedethat killed 126 people.
Dutch explorerPieter Nuytswas appointedgovernor of Formosa(modern-day Taiwan) by theDutch East India Company.
American serial killerJohn Wayne Gacywas executed bylethal injectionfor the murders of twelve teenage boys and young men in a series of killings committed between 1972 and 1978.
As part ofNazi Germany's persecution of transgender people, thousands of books taken from theInstitute for Sexual Sciencewere burned inBebelplatz squarefor being "un-German".
British prime ministerNeville Chamberlainresigned and formally recommendedWinston Churchillas his successor.
A land dispute between theSouthern Pacific Railroadand settlers inHanford, California, turned deadly whena gun battlebroke out, leaving seven dead.
In response to a 28-percent wage cut, 4,000Pullman Palace Car Companyworkerswent on strikeinIllinois, bringing rail traffic west of Chicago to a halt.
After aweek-long standoff punctuated by military clashes, Japanese forces captured the city ofJinan,Shandongin China.
India began thePokhran-IInuclear-weapons test, its first since theSmiling Buddhatest 24 years earlier.
Two car bombs by unknown perpetratorsexplodedinReyhanlı, Turkey, resulting in 52 killed and 140 injured.
TheDonner Party, anAmerican pioneergroup which became known for resorting tocannibalismwhen they became trapped in theSierra Nevada, leftIndependence, Missouri, for California.
The crew of the airshipNorge, led byRoald Amundsen, became the first people to make a verified trip to theNorth Pole.
Nazi deputies assaulted journalist Helmuth Klotz in the German parliament building after hepublicized the homosexualityof a senior Nazi politician.
German engineerKonrad Zusepresented theZ3, the first workingprogrammableand fully automaticcomputer, to an audience of scientists in Berlin.
TheJimi Hendrix Experiencereleased the critically acclaimed and widely influential debut albumAre You Experienced.
The Cambodian navyseizedthe American container shipSSMayaguezin what they claimed to be Cambodian territorial waters.
TheCoppergate Helmet(pictured), the best preserved of the six knownAnglo-Saxonhelmets, was discovered.
InPostville, Iowa,U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcementconductedthe largest-ever raidof a workplace and arrested nearly 400immigrantsforidentity theftand document fraud.
During an exercise to demonstrate air power,United States Army Air Corpsbomber aircraftinterceptedthe Italian ocean linerSSRex(pictured)620 nautical miles (1,100 km) off the US Atlantic coast.
The United Kingdom publicly announced that it wasindependently developing nuclear weapons, after the USAtomic Energy Act of 1946ended cooperation on the matter.
Four studentswere shot and killedby Indonesian soldiers atTrisakti UniversityinJakarta, which led towidespread riotsandthe resignationof PresidentSuhartonine days later.
The Australian astronomerJohn Tebbuttdiscovered theGreat Comet of 1861, through whose tail the Earth passed later that year.
The Russian inventorIgor Sikorskyflew the self-designedRussky Vityaz, the world's first four-enginefixed-wing aircraft.
The Australian adventurerBen Carlinbecame the only person tocircumnavigatethe world in anamphibious vehicle, having travelled over 80,000 kilometres (50,000 miles) by land and sea.
Eleven members of the AmericanBlack liberationgroupMOVEwere killed when aPhiladelphia policehelicopter dropped a bomb on their house during a raid.
US vice presidentRichard Nixon's motorcadewas attacked by a mobin Caracas, Venezuela.
Nine bombs placed by theIndian Mujahideen, then an unknown terrorist group,exploded in a 15-minute periodinJaipur, India, killing 80 people and injuring more than 200 others.
Led byMeriwether LewisandWilliam Clark, theCorps of DiscoveryleftCamp Duboisnear present-dayHartford, Illinois, to beginthe first overland expeditionto theWest Coast of the United Statesand back.
MajorHenry C. Waynearrived inIndianola, Texas, with 34 camels to form the short-livedUnited States Camel Corps(pictured).
Thelast witchcraft trialin the United States opened inSalem, Massachusetts.
InLima, Peru,Lina Medinabecame the youngest confirmed mother in history, giving birth at the age of five years, seven months and twenty-one days.
Trains ran on theTalyllyn RailwayinWalesfor the first time since itspreservation, making it the first railway in the world to be operated by volunteers.
On the day ofthe UEFA Cup Final,violence eruptedbetweenfootball hooligansupporters of both teams and theGreater Manchester Police, resulting in 39 arrests and 39 injured officers.
British politicianStephen Timmssurvived amurder attemptby anIslamic extremistduring aconstituency surgery.
Five people were killed inÅdalen, Sweden, assoldiers opened fire on an unarmed trade union demonstration.
Early English explorerBartholomew Gosnoldarrived onCape Codin present-dayMassachusetts.
English astronomerFrancis BailyobservedBaily's beads(example pictured), a phenomenon during asolar eclipsein which the rugged topography of thelunar limballows sunlight to shine through.
During a match, baseball starTy Cobbenters the stands and assaults a fan who had heckled him, leading tohis suspension.
TheBritish Armydirected fleeingCroatian soldiersto surrender to theYugoslav Partisans, beginning theBleiburg repatriations.
Don Murphy organized the firstpinewood derby, an event forCub Scoutsof theBoy Scouts of Americawhere wooden cars built by the scouts are raced.
The United Kingdom tested its firsthydrogen bomboverMalden IslandinOperation Grapple.
Disapproving of GeneralTôn Thất Đính'shandling of theBuddhist Uprising, South Vietnamese prime ministerNguyễn Cao Kỳordered an attack on his forces and ousted Đính from his post.
Policeopened fireduring a confrontation with a group ofJackson State Collegestudents, killing two students and injuring twelve others.
TheRyukyu Islandswere returned to Japan by the United States, and theU.S. occupation governmentwas abolished.
Three days before her seventeenth birthday,Jessica Watsonarrived inSydneyafter sailing non-stop andunassistedaround the world.
TheConference of Dresdenbegan, an attempt byNapoleonto secure support forhis planned invasion of Russia.
ProspectorJuan Godoydiscovered a silveroutcropinChañarcillo, sparking theChilean silver rush.
The United States Congress authorized the minting of theShield nickel(example pictured), the country's firstfive-cent pieceto be made of acopper–nickel alloy.

TheSedition Actwas passed in the United States, forbidding Americans from using "disloyal, profane, scurrilous, or abusive language" aboutthe government,flag, orarmed forcesduring the ongoing World War I.
The first modern performance ofClaudio Monteverdi's operaIl ritorno d'Ulisse in patriaoccurred in Paris.
TheLockheedF-104Starfighter, a supersonicinterceptor aircraft, set a worldflight airspeed recordof 1,404.012 mph (2,259.538 km/h).
TheTritons' FountaininValletta, one of Malta's most importantModernistlandmarks, was turned on for the first time.
American physicistTheodore Maimanoperated the first workinglaseratHughes Research LaboratoriesinMalibu.
Led byPark Chung-hee, the Military Revolution Committee carried outa bloodless coupagainst the government ofYun Posunin Seoul, ending theSecond Republic of Korea.
Based on the results of a referendum held about one month earlier, theKingdom of Sikkim(flag pictured)abolished its monarchy and was annexed to become the22nd state of India.
The firstChuck E. Cheeselocation, the firstfamily restaurantto integrate food,animated entertainment(example pictured), and an indoorarcade, opened inSan Jose, California.
At least 12 people were killed and 70 others injured whentwo bombs explodedin a market inNairobi, Kenya.
After a scuffle in which onecardinalhad several bones broken,a papal conclaveconvened in Rome elected Camillo Borghese asPope Paul V.
Thefirst Academy Awards ceremonywas held at theHollywood Roosevelt Hotelin Los Angeles, California.
Japanese climberJunko Tabei(pictured)became the first woman to reach the summit ofMount Everest.
TheInternational Telecommunication Union, which standardizes and regulates internationalradioandtelecommunications, was founded as the International Telegraph Union in Paris.
The operaCavalleria rusticanabyPietro Mascagni, premieres at theTeatro CostanziinRome, beginning theverismoperiod in Italian opera.
TheAntikythera mechanism, the oldest known survivinggearedmechanism, was discovered among artifacts retrieved froma shipwreckoff the Greek island ofAntikythera.
Under theProtocol of Corfu, thePrincipality of Albaniaofficially recognizedNorthern Epirusas an autonomous self-governing region.

After renegotiating a contract with the makers of her signature perfumeChanel No. 5,Coco Chanel(pictured)received a share of wartime profits from its sale, making her one of the richest women in the world.
Six-year-oldGedhun Choekyi Nyima, the11th Panchen Lamaselected by the14th Dalai Lama, was kidnapped by the Chinese government, who advocateda proxy.
Followingthe killing of two English football fansbyGalatasaraysupporters in the previous month, British and Turkishhooligansrioted on the dayofthe UEFA Cup Finalin Copenhagen, Denmark.
UEFA Cup Final riotsappears onMay 14, so 2000 riots should not appear in the same year
The first copies of the children's novelThe Wonderful Wizard of OzbyL. Frank Baumwere printed.

TheU.S. Supreme Courtruled in the landmark caseBrown v. Board of Education, outlawingracial segregationinpublic schoolsbecause "separate educational facilities are inherently unequal" and therefore unconstitutional.
An Iraqi jetfired two Exocet missilesat the American frigateUSSStark, killing 37 personnel and injuring 21 others.
Ruling in thelandmark decisionPlessy v. Ferguson, theU.S. Supreme Courtupheld the legality ofracial segregationinpublic transportationunder the "separate but equal" doctrine.

U.S. presidentFranklin D. Rooseveltsigned an act establishing theTennessee Valley Authorityto stimulate theeconomic developmentof theTennessee Valley, a region particularly impacted by theGreat Depression.
In a crime that captivated Japan,Sada Abe(pictured)strangled her lover, cut off his genitals, and carried them around with her for several days until her arrest.
The Soviet Unionforcibly deportedhundreds of thousands ofCrimean Tatarsto theUzbek SSRand elsewhere in the country.
India conductedits first nuclear test explosionatPokhran, the first confirmed nuclear test by a nation outside the five permanent members of theUnited Nations Security Council.
TheParliament of Nepalunanimously votedto strip KingGyanendraof many of his powers.
Mark Carson, an openly gay man,was murderedin a hate crime incident in New York City, prompting a 1,500-person march against anti-LGBTQ violence.

Disgruntledschool boardtreasurerAndrew Kehoeset off explosives with timers and a rifle(aftermath pictured), causing theBath School disasterin theBathConsolidated School inMichigan, killing 44 people in the deadliestmass murderin a school in United States history.
TheSri Lanka ArmykilledVelupillai Prabhakaran, the leader and founder of theLiberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam, to bring an end to the 26-yearSri Lankan civil war.
A combination of thick smoke, fog, and heavy cloud covercaused darknessto fall on parts of Canada and theNew Englandarea of the United States by noon.

CaptainJohn Franklin(pictured)departedGreenhithe, England, onan expeditionto theCanadian Arcticin search of theNorthwest Passage; all 129 men were later lost when their ships became icebound inVictoria Strait.
TheSierra Gorda Biosphere, which encompasses the mostecologically diverseregion in Mexico, was established as a result ofgrassrootsefforts.
In Bangkok, theThai military(pictured)concludeda week-long crackdownonwidespread protestsby forcing the surrender ofoppositionleaders.
A corroded pipeline nearRefugio State Beach, California,spilled 142,800 gallons (3,400 barrels) of crude oilonto theGaviota Coast.
French physicistJean-Pierre Christinpublished the design of amercury thermometerusing thecentigrade scale, with 0 representing themelting pointof water and 100 itsboiling point.
TheUnited States Congresspassedthe largest tariff in the nation's history, which resulted in severe economic hardship in the American South.
Ulysses, who would be famouslydepicted in a posthumous woodcut, landed in Lisbon, becoming the first of his species to visit Europe in a thousand years.
A British squadron underCharles Marsh Schombergdefeated a French forceoffTamatave, Madagascar, that was attempting to reinforce the French garrison onMauritius.

Representatives from seventeen countries signed theMetre Convention, which set up an institute for the purpose of coordinating internationalmetrologyand for coordinating the development of themetric system.
By theTreaty of Jeddah, the United Kingdom recognised the sovereignty of KingAbdulaziz of Saudi Arabia(pictured)overHejazandNejd, which later merged to become Saudi Arabia.
TheLuttra Woman, abog bodyfrom the EarlyNeolithicperiod, was discovered nearLuttra, Sweden.
The first session of theNational Dietopened in Tokyo, Japan.
While attempting to land atCairo International Airport,Pakistan International Airlines Flight 705crashed for unknown reasons, killing all but 6 of the 121 people on board.
In decidingRomer v. Evans, theU.S. Supreme Courtstruck down a constitutional amendment inColoradothat preventedprotected statusunder the law for homosexuals or bisexuals.
The first oftwo major earthquakesstruck Northern Italy, resulting in seven deaths.
With the signing of theTreaty of Jeddah, the United Kingdom recognized the sovereignty ofIbn SaudoverHejazandNejd, which later merged to become Saudi Arabia.
English writerDaniel Defoewas imprisoned forseditious libelafter publishinga pamphletthat was perceived to satirise theTorypublications aboutDissenters.
TheCongress of Colombiapassed a law abolishingslavery in the country, to take effect at the beginning of the new year.
A crowd of about 800 pro-slavery Americansransackedthe town ofLawrence, Kansas.

Mexican presidentPorfirio Díazand the revolutionaryFrancisco I. Maderosigned theTreaty of Ciudad Juárezto end hostilities between each other's forces, concluding the initial phase of theMexican Revolution.
TheImperial War Graves Commissionwas established byroyal charterto mark, record and maintain the graves and places of commemoration ofBritish Empiremilitary forces.

Aboard theSpirit of St. Louis, American aviatorCharles Lindbergh(pictured)completed the first solo non-stoptransatlantic flight, flying fromRoosevelt Fieldnear New York City toParis–Le Bourget Airport.
While working with a mass ofplutoniumknown as thedemon core,Manhattan ProjectphysicistLouis Slotinaccidentally exposed himself to a lethal dose ofhard radiation.
Former Indian prime ministerRajiv Gandhiwasassassinated by a suicide bomberinSriperumbudur, Tamil Nadu.
Indonesian presidentSuhartoresigned aftera collapse of support for his presidencyamid economic and political crises, ending 32 years in power.
The world's tallestroller coaster,Kingda Ka, opened atSix Flags Great AdventureinJackson, New Jersey, U.S.
TheManchester Ship Canal, linkingManchesterinNorth West Englandto theIrish Sea, officially opened, becoming the world's largest navigation canal at the time.
The operaDoktor Faust, unfinished when composerFerruccio Busoni(pictured)died, was premieredin Dresden.
A Taiwanese mancarried out a stabbing spreeon aTaipei Metrotrain, killing four people and injuring 24 others.
TheTrevi Fountain(pictured)in Rome was officially inaugurated byPope Clement XIII.
InShiraz, Iran, theBábdeclared himself to be a messenger of God toMullá Husayn, leading to the foundation ofBábism, considered to be a precursor to theBaháʼí Faith.
SenatorCharles Sumner(pictured)was assaultedby RepresentativePreston Brooksin theUnited States Senate chamberin retaliation for a speech in which Sumner fiercely criticized slaveholders.
The firstBlackwall Tunnelunder theRiver Thameswas opened to improve commerce and trade in theEast End of London.
SultanAbdul Hamid IIestablished theUllah millet, a separatemilletfor theAromanianswithin theOttoman Empire.
California'sLassen Peakviolently erupted, the onlyvolcanic eruptionin thecontiguous U.S.in the 20th century untilMount St. Helenserupted in 1980.
Germany and Italy signed thePact of Steel, a military and political alliance.
TheDominion of Ceylonchanged its name toSri Lanka, adopted a new constitution, and officially became arepublic within the Commonwealth.
Location testing forPac-Man, a Japanesearcade gamethat became an icon of 1980spopular culture, began inShibuya, Tokyo.
DuringHindu–Muslim riotinginMeerut, India, 19 members of theProvincial Armed Constabularyallegedlymassacred42 Muslims and dumped their bodies in water canals.
Police announced that the skeletal remains ofFederal Bureau of PrisonsinternChandra Levy, who had been missing for a year, had been found inRock Creek Parkin Washington, D.C.
Upon landing inMangalore,Air India Express Flight 812overshot the runway and fell down a hillside, killing 158 of the 166 people on board.
eruption of Mount St. Helensappears onMay 18, so Lassen Peak should not appear in the same year
Thai military crackdownappears onMay 19, so 2014 coup should not appear in the same year
InPublic Prosecutor v Taw Cheng Kong, theCourt of Appeal of Singaporeoverruled aHigh Courtdecision in the only time a statute in Singapore had been ruled unconstitutional.
Gian Pietro Carafa becamePope Paul IV, beginning a tumultuous four-year papacy during which thePapal Statessuffered a serious military defeat.
Backed bySamuel J. Tilden, theAstor Libraryand theLenox Libraryagreed to merge and form theNew York Public Library.
The U.S. Navy submarineSqualussank offPortsmouth, New Hampshire, during tests, causing 26 men to drown.
TheAirbus A300, the first twin-enginedwide-bodyairliner, went into service withAir France.
TheInternational Court of Justiceawarded theMiddle Rocksto Malaysia andPedra Brancato Singapore, resolvinga 29-year-old territorial disputein theSingapore Strait.
TheDutch Revoltbroke out when rebels led byLouis of Nassau(pictured)invadedFrieslandat theBattle of Heiligerlee.
TheNorth-West Mounted Police, the forerunner of theRoyal Canadian Mounted Police, was established to bring law and order to and assert Canadian sovereignty over theNorthwest Territories.
Duringa strike against the Electric Auto-Lite companyinToledo, a fight began between nearly 10,000 American strikers and sheriff's deputies, later involving theOhio National Guard.
Professional wrestlerOwen Hartdied immediately beforea World Wrestling Federation matchafter dropping 70 feet (21 m) onto the ring during a botched entrance.
Chateau Montelena Chardonnay
Led byKing Louis XIV, the French army invaded theSpanish Netherlands, beginning theWar of Devolution.
At aMoravianmeeting inAldersgate, London,John Wesley(pictured)experienced aspiritual rebirth, leading him to launch theMethodist movement.
Thenursery rhyme"Mary Had a Little Lamb" was first published as a poem bySarah Josepha Hale.
New York City'sBrooklyn Bridgeopened as thelongest suspension bridge in the worldat the time.
English aviatorAmy Johnsonlanded inDarwin, becoming the first woman to fly solo from England to Australia.
Thefirst editionof theEurovision Song Contestwas held inLugano, Switzerland.

On theKola Peninsulain Russia, drilling began on theKola Superdeep Borehole, which eventually reached a depth of 12,262 metres (40,230 ft), making it the deepestboreholeever drilled and thelowest artificial point on Earth.
In awine competitionin Paris, French judgesshocked the wine industryby ratingCalifornia wineshigher thanFrench ones.
Astationary frontbegan over the central Caribbean Sea,leading to severe floodsthat over two weeks killed dozens of people in Cuba, the Dominican Republic, Haiti and Jamaica.
TheIsrael Defense ForcesbeganOperation Solomon, acovert operationto bring thousands ofEthiopian Jewsto Israel(evacuees pictured).
Valdivia earthquakeappears onMay 22, so Puyehue-Cordón Caulle should not appear in the same year
The mentally ill KingErik XIVof Sweden(pictured)and his guardsmurdered five incarcerated nobles, including some members of the influentialSturefamily.
TheAct of Tolerationbecame law, grantingfreedom of worshipto Englishnonconformistsunder certain circumstances, but deliberately excluding Catholics.
TheIrish Rebellion of 1798began, with battles beginning inCounty Kildareand fighting later spreading across the country.
United States Attorney GeneralRobert F. Kennedymet withAfrican American authorJames Baldwinin an unsuccessful attempt to improve race relations.
A gunman involved inIslamic extremismopened fireat theJewish Museum of Belgiumin Brussels, killing four people.
poster forH.M.S. Pinafore
TheConstitutional Conventionmet inPhiladelphiawith the intention of revising theArticles of Confederationof the United States.
The poemsKubla KhanandChristabelby English poetSamuel Taylor Coleridge(pictured)were published.
Employees of theRemington Randcompany began an11-month strike action, during which time the company executives developed the notorious "Mohawk Valley formula" to intimidate the strikers.
TheWehrmachtand theircollaborationistallies launchedOperation Rösselsprung, a failed attempt to assassinate theYugoslav PartisanleaderJosip Broz Tito.

In an address toCongress, U.S. presidentJohn F. Kennedyannounced his support for theApollo program, with "the goal, before this decade is out, of landing a man on the Moon and returning him safely to the Earth".
TheBaltimore Steam Packet Company, the last overnightsteamboatservice in the United States, went out of business.
Six-year-oldEtan Patz disappearedon his way to school in New York City, and later became one of the first missing children to havehis picture featured on milk cartons.

During takeoff fromO'Hare International Airportin Chicago, an engine detached fromAmerican Airlines Flight 191, causing a crash that killed 273 people in the deadliest aviation accident in United States history.
North Koreaconducted a nuclear testand several other missile tests that were widely condemned internationally and led to sanctions from theUnited Nations Security Council.
The final episode ofThe Oprah Winfrey Show, the highest-rated daytimetalk showinU.S. televisionhistory, was broadcast.
Ina test flight,SpaceX'sDragonbecame the first commercial spacecraft to rendezvous and berth with theInternational Space Station.
ThePrimera Junta, the first independent government in Argentina, was established in anopen cabildoinBuenos Aires, marking the end of theMay Revolution.
